IncidentBot: PAGER: elevated inference 5xx rate observed from eu-central-1a -> alert: inference.errors.region.eu-central-1a > 3%
PD-Bot: paging oncall -> @Sofia Oncall
Sofia Oncall: on it. seeing spike in 5xx and a cluster of model load failures in eu-central-1a. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/graph?alert=inf-err-euc1a (graphs)
Ravi Infra: digging into node logs. IMDS GETs are timing out/503ing from sidecars; sidecar fails to refresh STS creds -> S3 returns 403 when fetching model weights.
Jamie SRE: example logs from a failed load:
```
2026-03-15T12:08:14Z runtime-sidecar ERROR fetch-creds GET http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ timed out (attempt 3)
2026-03-15T12:08:21Z model-loader ERROR s3 GET s3://redwood-models/gpt-v2.tar failed status=403 requestid=XXXXX
```
Maya Runtime: that fits: model-loader uses IMDS to get short-lived creds for S3. If IMDS is flaky, model pulls fail and nodes that need to load a model return 5xx. This is not an ENI or NAT issue.
Sofia Oncall: mitigation plan options:
- steer traffic away from eu-central-1a ASAP
- trigger local-cache fallback on nodes that have model artifacts on disk
- if needed, failover requests to eu-west-1 replicas (higher latency but fewer errors)
Sam Support: CS seeing customer reports for eu-central endpoints. I'll issue a preliminary customer note.
Ravi Infra: starting traffic steering now. running: 
```
# set routing weight to zero for the AZ
redwoodctl routing update --zone eu-central-1a --weight 0.0 --reason "IMDS timeouts -> model load failures"
```
Jamie SRE: also issuing on-host fallback command where cache exists:
```
for h in $(cat affected_hosts.txt); do ssh $h 'sudo systemctl restart runtime-sidecar && sudo -u redwood /opt/redwood/bin/preload-models --use-local-cache'; done
```
Maya Runtime: pushed a small hotfix to model-loader to preferentially use local cached credentials file if available (will reduce dependency on IMDS for short-term). Rolling canary 10% now.
IncidentBot: rollout r-5678 started (canary 10%)
PD-Bot: AWS SR #123456789 opened and assigned to Ravi (cc: eng). AWS initial reply: "We see elevated latencies and errors from the AZ metadata service; internal mitigation in progress." ETA unknown.
Sofia Oncall: customer impact estimate: approx 3.8% of hosted inference requests in eu-central-1 returned 5xx between 12:06–12:44 UTC. Dedicated tenants pinned to the AZ experienced model load errors until fallbacks were applied.
Alex Eng: KV cache remains healthy; this is primarily model load/auth failures. After routing change we see tail latency drop but a small subset of nodes still 5xx due to unloaded models.
Jamie SRE: monitoring: errors started dropping at 12:20 UTC after routing steer + cache fallback, trending to baseline by 12:38. keeping watch.
Maya Runtime: follow-ups (for postmortem):
- (P0) implement persistent credential cache and fallback in model-loader (owner: Maya, PR #2345)
- (P1) pre-warm critical model artifacts across zones during deploys (owner: Alex)
- (P1) add IMDS error rate alert and runbook (owner: Jamie)
- (P2) coordinate with AWS to get root cause and consider cross-AZ metadata proxy improvements (owner: Ravi)
Sofia Oncall: handing off monitoring to @Jamie SRE for 2h watch. I'll prepare incident summary and schedule postmortem. Thanks all for fast response :clap:
Sam Support: posting customer update: "We observed transient failures in eu-central-1a impacting model loads. We routed traffic away from the affected AZ and applied fallbacks; customers may see a slight increase in latency while we recovered. We'll follow up with a detailed RCA." :thumbsup:
Ravi Infra: AWS updated SR: "We applied internal mitigation; metadata proxy request success rate improving. Recommend keeping traffic away from affected AZ for 30–60 minutes while we validate."
Sofia Oncall: closing pager, channel remains open for handoff. Will create incident ticket and assign action items.
